title: Metaphysical Consciousness Architecture
definition: The abstract framework that explains the interaction between consciousness and physical bodies, incorporating concepts such as rebirth, past lives, enlightenment, and trauma healing.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine consciousness as a software that can run on different hardware, like a computer. This software can access data from its past runs, which can influence its current behavior. Sometimes, it might mix with data from another, unrelated software run, just like your phone can mix apps.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Metaphysical consciousness architecture refers to the theoretical model that utilizes the Object Storage Tree (OSTree) model to explain phenomena such as rebirth, past lives, enlightenment, and trauma healing. It suggests that consciousness can be accessed and influenced by data from past experiences, similar to how a read-only terminal session can provide insights from a pinned deployment.
difficulty_levels.expert: The metaphysical consciousness architecture is a philosophical framework that proposes a hypervisor-level interaction between consciousness and physical bodies. It draws from the Object Storage Tree (OSTree) model, distributed version control, and containerization to explain phenomena such as rebirth, past lives, enlightenment, trauma healing, and ancestral trauma. This framework also introduces the concept of DNA as a biological, hardware-level repository of ancestral and karmic reference data, providing a biological explanation for phobias and talents.

extra_fields.insight: The metaphysical consciousness architecture provides a cross-compatible, internally consistent framework for explaining phenomena such as rebirth, past lives, enlightenment, and trauma healing using the terminology of distributed version control and containerization.
